title: agency-level-fatal-OIS: Agency-year counts of people shot and killed by police, with the protocol v1.0 sample (v1.0)
description:
Annual counts of people shot and killed by on-duty police officers, by U.S. law enforcement agency, going back as far as sources allow (1969 for Chicago). Hand-built series for 438 agencies sit beside four national sources keyed to the same FBI ORI codes: The Washington Post's Fatal Force (2015-2024), Fatal Encounters (2000-2021), Mapping Police Violence (2013-2025), and the FBI's Supplementary Homicide Reports (1976-2024). The merged panel covers 4,624 agencies and 145,657 agency-years.

This release completes the collection fixed by the pre-registered protocol (version 1.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24248721): pre-1995 counts for all 56 agencies in its stratified draw, rebuilt case by case from local newspapers, with a recall check for each agency. It includes the protocol's analysis (scripts/09_sample_analysis.R). Of the 56 agencies, 54 enter the comparison and 52 have at least one death. Pooled across agencies, fatal police shootings in 2015-2025 are about where they were in 1985-1994 (ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.69-1.35; per resident 0.83, 0.61-1.13). The typical agency kills about twice as many people a year now (2.01, 1.40-2.89; per resident 1.71, 1.28-2.27). The Supplementary Homicide Reports record 94% of the deaths counted here before 1995 but 56% since 2015. Departures from the protocol are listed in the README.

Every newspaper-sourced death is logged with its source in data/historical/historical_ois_evidence.csv. Fatal Encounters, Mapping Police Violence, the Supplementary Homicide Reports, and the Law Enforcement Agency Identifiers Crosswalk are linked rather than redistributed; data/README.md says where to get each. Code is MIT-licensed; data are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, because the panel adapts The Washington Post's Fatal Force data.
